sentences.text: The facts of the case are that the Food Inspector A.K. Dubey found the revisionist on 18.5.1999 at about 11.00 a.m. while he was selling milk in a container which was intended for sale.
The food Inspector introduced himself to the accused and asked license for sale to which he denied.

The complainant purchased 750 ml. milk by giving Rs.6/-for sample and then kept in three bottles in equal quantity after mixing 40% formalin of 20-20 drops each was added for preserving it which was then sent to the public analyst for chemical analysis who by his report dated 26.6.1999 reported it to be adulterated as it contained 96% less milk fat and 40% less milk solid non-fat in it.
The complainant then took sanction from the C.M.O. concerned and filed a complaint against the revisionist/accused.
In the trial court the complainant A.K. Dubey, Food Inspector, was examined as P.W.-1 under Section 244 Cr.P.C. and Har Prasad, Food Clerk, was examined as P.W.-2 under Section 246 Cr.P.C.
The accused/revisionist in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated of false implication.
The trial court convicted and sentenced the accused/revisionist as stated above.
The appeal was preferred against the same which came to be dismissed and thereafter the present revision has been filed against both the impugned judgement and orders.

7. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that the prosecution against the revisionist is bad in the eyes of law inasmuch as the notice under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has not been received by the revisionist.

It is argued that as per the prosecution case the sample of mixed milk is alleged to have been taken on 18.5.1999 and the report of the Food Analyst is dated 26.6.1999 but the witness P.W.-2 who was the food clerk states of sending the same to the revisionist through a registered post dated 21.07.1999.
The said postal receipt has been filed by him and proved by him which is marked as Exhibit No. Ka-8 to the trial court's record.

It is argued there is nothing on record to show that the said report has been received by the revisionist and the statement that mere dispatch of the report to the accused is not a sufficient compliance of the requirement of Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 as there has to be a positive evidence that the report has been served on the accused.

He has placed reliance on the judgments of the Apex Court in the cases of Vijendra Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh: (2020) 15 SCC 763 (para-14 and 15) and Narayan Prasad Sahu Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh: (2022) 1 SCC 87 (para-5, 6, 8 and 9).

entities.text: Vijendra Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh: (2020) 15 SCC 763
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Narayan Prasad Sahu Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh: (2022) 1 SCC 87
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued that as such a prosecution against the revisionist is bad in the eyes of law.

It is argued that the delay in the present matter from the side of the prosecution is enormous inasmuch as the sample of the food item was alleged to be taken by the Food Inspector on 18.05.1999 after which it was analysed and a report was given by the public analyst on 26.06.1999 but then the complaint was filed on 20.07.1999 which is after about two months of the date of taking of the sample and after which it is stated that the notice under Section 13(2) of the Act was sent on 21.07.1999 which is after about two months from the date of taking of the sample.
It is argued that the available right of the revisionist-accused for getting the sample re-tested from the Central Food Laboratory is totally affected.
The present revision, thus, be allowed and the judgments and orders impugned be set aside.

Rajpal vs State Of U.P. on 9 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129732444/
2 8.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and arguments and argued that the trial court has given cogent reasons for convicting the revisionist.
The appellate court has also considered the matter in its true prospective and has come to a conclusion that the appeal deserves to be dismissed.

9. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that in the present case notice was sent to revisionist but there is nothing on record to show that the said notice was served upon the revisionist.
The purpose of Section under Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954 is defeated.
On the said count the prosecution of the revisionist is bad in the eyes of law which deserves to be set-aside.
10. The present revision is allowed.
The impugned judgement and order dated 30.6.2011, passed by Addl. Sessions Judge, Court No.6, Budaun and the impugned judgement and order dated 17.8.2007 passed by Second Addl.
